scenes.headline: WATER TANK?
scenes.text: So why give a weapon a water-container name?

scenes.headline: LATE 1915
scenes.text: You're guarding a secret British project in late nineteen fifteen.

scenes.headline: CROSS THE TRENCHES
scenes.text: Engineers want a machine that can cross trenches and smash through wire.

scenes.headline: TOO OBVIOUS
scenes.text: But a name like 'landship' tells the enemy too much.

scenes.headline: COVER NAME
scenes.text: So the project gets an innocent cover name: tank.

scenes.headline: SOUNDS HARMLESS
scenes.text: Not because it carries water. Because it's supposed to sound like it does.

scenes.headline: FAKE DESTINATION
scenes.text: Some are even marked in Russian: 'With care to Petrograd.'

scenes.headline: WILL IT WORK?
scenes.text: But would this secret weapon actually work?

scenes.headline: 15 SEP 1916
scenes.text: In September nineteen sixteen, it goes into battle at Flers. Forty-nine tanks are assigned. Only thirty-two reach the start line.

scenes.headline: 8 MEN INSIDE
scenes.text: Behind that harmless name are eight men going into battle.

scenes.headline: WATER TANK?
scenes.text: The secret ends. The harmless name survives. Would that cover story fool you?
